messages:
olivia: thinking about how we surface automatic fallback decisions in the console — want design that helps SREs and PMs understand why traffic moved and whether it was correct. quick sketch below and a few questions.

sam: +1. we should show a compact timeline on the route page: green=normal, amber=soft-degrade, red=hard-degrade. click to expand event details.

olivia: agree on timeline. what fields do we need in the event detail? my list: timestamp, trigger (error/latency/quota), matched rule id, previous model, fallback variant, sample request id, telemetry snapshot. anything missing?

marta: audit needs decision reason + human-readable rule match. also need an immutable compact snapshot of the input (truncated) and output diff if available. retention rules are important — default 90d but configurable.

kevin: small API nit: the fallback decision should be returned to the console via the internal /route-events stream with a stable schema. propose we add a header to internal responses for tracing: `X-Rw-Fallback: reason=high_latency;variant=small-quant` so logs and traces can correlate.

sam: caution exposing to external callers. internal header only on platform plane; UI should fetch richer context from the events API.

anya: product note: surface the most recent N fallback events on the route overview + a single-click "Replay" that reruns the sample request against the pinned model and the fallback model side-by-side. helps validate whether fallback was appropriate.

olivia: UI idea: event detail tabs — Summary | Telemetry | Trace | Repro. Telemetry shows percentile latency, error breakdown, token counts, and route quota usage at trigger time. Trace links to our trace viewer. Repro gives the request JSON and buttons: replay / snapshot-to-eval / open-in-playground.

marta: security: snapshot-to-eval must scrub PII by default and require a policy tag to retain raw payloads. also add an HSM-backed audit signing event id for legal compliance.

kevin: quick implementation sketch for the fallback event payload (internal):
```json
{
  "event_id":"ev_...",
  "route":"/v1/generate",
  "ts":1915554321,
  "trigger":"error_rate>0.05",
  "matched_rule":"policy-43",
  "action":"switch_model",
  "from":"gptx-large-v3",
  "to":"gptx-small-quant",
  "sample_request_id":"req_123",
  "telemetry_snapshot":"s3://dots/telemetry/ev_..."
}
```

olivia: that looks good. small ask: include `decision_path` array so we can render the bulletized reasoning (e.g., ["latency>99th","region=us-east-1","quota=overcommit"]).

sam: UX/ops debate: should we show automatic fallback reasons to end customers (via response header) or keep it platform-only? Ops says show it as `X-Redwood-Fallback` to help debugging; legal says no leak. needs product decision.

anya: product preference: platform-only by default. expose to customers only when tenant opts in and signs SLA that allows revealing variant info. add an account-level toggle.

kevin: ok. last question: do we allow manual override from the event detail ("force back to primary") or only via rollout controls? ops wants quick escape hatch in route page.

marta: prefer controlled rollback flow that requires a ticket or 2FA when in enterprise mode. for self-serve routes allow quick toggle but record an audit entry.

olivia: implementation timeline suggestion: P0: events API + schema, timeline in route page. P1: replay button + scrubbed snapshot. P2: replay-to-eval and signed audit retention. P3: tenant-facing header toggle. feedback? :eyes:

sam: :thumbsup: nice. I can take the events API proto.

kevin: I’ll add header gating and sign-off flow.

marta: I’ll write the audit retention + PII scrub spec.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.20 18:02 UTC — feature/ev-stream -> staging succeeded :rocket: 

olivia: thanks all — will update the mockups and post in #design once I have the timeline component ready.
